players.product: Power Systems division: backup engines and gas engines for prime power at data centres; next-generation engine to replace the Series 4000, targeting the data centre market with increased power density (launch 2028)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the 2026 Civil cash outlook: 2026 net LTSA balance growth is expected to be below the 2025 level, reflecting large engine flying hours towards the lower end of the 115% to 120% range of 2019 levels, a higher normalised engine flying hour rate, and shop visits growing to between 1,480 to 1,550 with more refurbs including Trent 1000s and XWBs, plus a higher level of catch-ups year-on-year.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 shop visits 1,480 to 1,550; large engine flying hours towards the lower end of 115% to 120% of 2019 levels

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the Trent 1000 XE has now been selected by three airlines including LATAM, welcomed back as a Trent 1000 XE customer, with several significant ongoing sales campaigns. CEO on the XWB-97: the improvement programme remains on track, and following the ground test programme Rolls-Royce will flight test and certify the enhanced engine next year ahead of a 2028 entry into service.
quarterly_data.figure: Trent 1000 XE selected by three airlines; XWB-97 enhanced engine entry into service 2028
